finding: After this round removed the stored clean-flag, §3.4's round-level 'wholly severity-less' rule (clean iff zero surviving findings) is computationally identical to applying §4.1's per-finding rule (missing/out-of-enum severity => treated as blocking) uniformly: in a wholly severity-less round every surviving finding is missing-severity and therefore blocking, so 'no blocking survives' equals 'zero survives'. §4.1 explicitly partitions the two as distinct domains, yet the round-level rule adds no behavior — the spec even concedes the result is identical under blocking and all. The special case, the mixed-round clarification, and Test 19's separate machinery are now dead weight (P3 Minimal Tokens).
suggestion: Drop the round-level severity-less special case and state one uniform rule: a surviving finding whose severity is missing or outside critical|high|medium|low is blocking (§4.1), applied to every round; cleanliness then follows from that single blocking predicate with no round-level partition, and §3.4 / Test 19 collapse to a reference to it.

finding: §4.1 treats a surviving finding 'whose severity is … outside critical|high|medium|low' as blocking, and §4.3 fixes the vocabulary as those four lowercase tokens, but neither §4.1 nor Test 19 states whether the severity match is case-sensitive. A value like 'MEDIUM' or 'Low' from an LLM reviewer is then indeterminate: under a case-sensitive read it is 'outside the set' → blocking → round not clean; under case-insensitive normalization it maps to medium/low → non-blocking → round clean. The two readings flip the clean flag (and nonblocking_open, §4.2) for the non-blocking severities, so two engineers writing Test 19 with a mixed-case medium/low severity assert opposite outcomes. (High/critical stay blocking either way, masking the divergence.)
suggestion: State in §4.1 whether severity comparison is case-sensitive: either 'severity is matched case-insensitively (normalized to lower-case before classifying)' or 'matched exactly; any non-lowercase spelling is outside the set and treated as blocking', and add a Test 19 case using a mixed-case medium/low severity pinning the resulting clean flag.

finding: §8.4 says under --compact next_action is 'trimmed to its runnable command atom (or the shortest directive where no command exists)', but branch-3's next_action (§8.2) is deliberately compound: it names two runnable commands in sequence (`tp set --workflow checks='[…]'` then `tp review <spec> --record <file>`) precisely so the loop keeps progressing rather than pinning at branch 3. 'Trimmed to its runnable command atom' is singular and does not say which of the two commands survives compaction; neither §8.4 clause covers a multi-command directive. Dropping either atom defeats branch 3's stated purpose (lose the check registration, or lose the progression to the next round), so the implementer must invent the compaction rule for the one compound branch.
suggestion: State how a compound directive compacts — e.g. keep both command atoms joined by 'then' (`tp set --workflow checks='[…]' then tp review <spec> --record <file>`) and drop only the parenthetical narration — so branch 3's register-then-record sequence survives --compact intact.

finding: §8.4 says under --compact next_action is 'trimmed to its runnable command atom (or the shortest directive where no command exists)', but §8.2 branch 3's next_action is a compound directive carrying TWO runnable commands: register the check (`tp set --workflow checks='[…]'`) and then the branch-4 `tp review <spec> --record <file>`. 'Its runnable command atom' (singular) does not say which survives. If only the record command survives, branch 3's compact output is indistinguishable from branch 4's and the check-registration step — the branch's entire purpose per Principle 6 and §8.1 ('next_action names the next-step command and check registration') — is silently dropped on the default-compact path where AX agents run.
suggestion: Specify branch 3's compact form explicitly: retain both command atoms (e.g. `tp set --workflow checks='[…]'; tp review <spec> --record <file>`), or state that the check-registration command is the atom kept, so the register signal is never lost under --compact and branch 3 stays distinguishable from branch 4.

finding: §8.4 says under --compact, next_action is 'trimmed to its runnable command atom (or the shortest directive where no command exists), dropping the procedural narration', but for the two compound branches this leaves the compact value unpinned. Branch 1 review (converged) is 'decompose the spec into tasks, then tp import <base>.tasks.json' and Branch 3 is 'register the check … then [run the next round]' — each mixes an agent-only action with a tp command. Trimming to 'the runnable command atom' would keep tp import / tp set --workflow and DROP the load-bearing agent step (decompose; the actual reason to advance), yet Test 14 characterizes Branch 1 as 'the decompose-then-tp import directive'. Test 18 only asserts next_action is 'retained' under --compact, never its exact compact string, and no test pins what the atom is for a command-bearing directive vs a directive-only branch (2 review). Two engineers would assert contradictory compact values.
suggestion: Pin the exact compact form of next_action for each of the four review branches (and the audit trio): for a command-bearing directive, either keep the full directive verbatim or specify the exact retained atom AND that the agent-action clause is preserved; add an assertion to Test 18 (or Test 14) giving the literal compact string per branch.

finding: The new --compact trimming rule in §8.4 gives next_action exactly two forms: 'its runnable command atom' or 'the shortest directive where no command exists'. But §8.2 branch 1 (converged review: 'decompose the spec into tasks, then tp import <base>.tasks.json') and branch 3 (register a check, then record another round) are classified by §8.2 as directives that ALSO embed a runnable tp command — a third case the binary rule does not cover. Read literally, branch 1 has a command, so it trims to the command atom `tp import <base>.tasks.json`, dropping the 'decompose the spec into tasks' prerequisite, which is essential agent work per §8.2 ('decomposition is the agent's work'), not the 'procedural narration the agent's workflow already prescribes' that §8.4 licenses dropping.
suggestion: In §8.4, state how compact trims a directive that embeds a command (branches 1 and 3): keep the essential directive verb plus the command atom and drop only surrounding narration, so the converged-review compact next_action stays 'decompose the spec into tasks, then tp import <base>.tasks.json' (or its shortest faithful form) rather than collapsing to `tp import <base>.tasks.json` alone.

finding: The round-level severity-less rule in §3.4 ('clean iff zero surviving' when no finding in the round carries a severity) yields the same result as applying §4.1's per-finding conservative-blocking rule (missing severity → blocking) to that same round: when every finding lacks severity, every surviving finding is blocking under `blocking`, and any survivor blocks under `all` (§3.3), so cleanliness collapses to 'zero surviving' either way. The special case therefore adds no observable behavior, and Test 19's asserted 'distinction' between the round-level rule and the per-finding rule is not observable — an implementer who implements only §4.1 per-finding (plus the §3.3 `all` definition) produces identical output for every input.
suggestion: Either drop the round-level severity-less rule and let it fall out of §4.1 + the §3.3 `all` definition, or, if kept for exposition, state explicitly that it is a derivable special case (not an independent predicate) so the implementer knows a single per-finding clean predicate suffices.

finding: §8.4 deliberately refuses to emit accepted_open because it is derivable from the clean flag + nonblocking_open, and §4.2 lets nonblocking_open's mere presence signal the accepted-open state (no companion boolean). §6.3 applies the opposite pattern to the harness feature: it emits harness_stale as an always-on boolean AND emits harness_note only when stale — so harness_stale:true is fully derivable from harness_note's presence, the very derivable-boolean the spec drops elsewhere. In non-compact output (the only mode where either appears; §8.4 strips both under --compact) harness_stale:false is emitted on every response as a no-op byte and harness_stale:true duplicates the presence signal harness_note already carries. Two adjacent new features thus use contradictory emission-economy rules, and the harness one spends a byte the spec's own §8.4 discipline says to derive.
suggestion: Pick one rule and apply it to both. Either (a) drop harness_stale and let harness_note's presence signal drift (matching nonblocking_open / the accepted_open decision), noting harness_note is emitted iff the two latest notes differ; or (b) explicitly justify in §6.3/§8.4 why the harness diagnostic keeps an always-on boolean while nonblocking/accepted_open do not, so the asymmetry is intentional rather than an oversight.
